channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Anger and frustration (scp article)" - A non anomalous man is contained by the foundation.

item.title: Re: Anger and frustration (scp article)
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this.

For the sake of comparison, consider SCP-4057. It sets out to do a very similar thing to what you're talking about but it's a tad "tighter", I guess would be the word. The meme is explained in the narrative, first of all, and it's tied into what happens when the non-anomalous person is contained.

What you've got here is an interesting setup — non-anomalous person in containment — but I'm not sensing a really cohesive story. Where'd this meme come from, why does it only affect the Foundation, why does it become this extreme, why is this person worthy of note, etc.

item.title: Re: Anger and frustration (scp article)
item.content:encoded:
PM Request. Placeholdered! Be right there! 👍

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Overall, I'm not really feeling this. 'Something compels people to do thing' is really overdone. Granted, any cliche can be overcome with a good enough story or execution enacted, but, 'non-anomalous man gets wrongly contained because compulsion' doesn't really have enough meat on its bones to take off.

I like the idea of a non-anomalous man being contained, however. There just needs to be a better reason. Also, considering the fact that this man has a Memetic effect that makes the Foundation want to contain him, isn't that Anomalous? Unless that's just the kicker you were going for.

However, even a bland anomaly can be done right with proper execution and a good enough attached story.

I recommend finding a way to make Kevin's anomaly a little less bland and one note and/or thinking of a good Narrative to strap to this. Do you aim for this to be funny? Sad? Anger-inducing? Personally, I see this being something that can be used for a -J ("Haha, normal man contained haha") but even then, the joke would get stale rather quickly.

Anywho, I hope so helped and I bid you a good day.

👍👍👍👍👍👍

item.title: Anger and frustration (scp article)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights yes

page type scp article

Elevator pitch: a memetic anomaly that effects foundation personnel, that makes them compelled to contain an ordinary man, who they believe to be anomalous.

Central narrative: A memetic anomaly that effects foundation staff, that deeply compels them to contain a man named Kevin. The anomalous qualities that the foundation assumes Kevin possesses constantly change, and no memory of previous research seems to be exhibited. Kevin of course, is immensely stressed, and is desperate to get out of this situation, although he's resigns himself to the fact that that's probably not going to happen.

hook/Attention grabber: the foundations obsession with finding something anomalous. An innocent person being contained.
